source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: What mechanism does the lecture point to for why an earlier graded submission can bias the grading of a later one in the same chat conversation?

options.text: Attention -- everything said earlier in the conversation can influence what the model generates next
options.feedback: The lecture ties this directly to attention: because a model draws on everything earlier in the conversation when producing new output, an earlier grading can shift how a later submission comes out, for better or worse.

options.text: Sampling randomness -- each grade differs slightly by chance
options.feedback: Random sampling would produce small, undirected variation, not a systematic bias toward harsher or more lenient grading based on what came right before. The lecture points to context carrying forward, not chance.

options.text: Post-training -- the reinforcement-learning stage makes the model grade every submission identically
options.feedback: Post-training shapes the model once, before any conversation happens; it cannot explain why grading drifts within a single ongoing chat. The bias described comes from what is currently in the conversation, not from training.

options.text: The harness -- providing files and memory lets the agent treat every submission identically
options.feedback: This actually describes the fix, not the problem. A harness giving each submission a fresh subagent is what prevents this bias; it is not the cause of it.
